summary: Four specific problems, none of them capacity. One measure recalculates an average for every customer (formula engine, 4,127 storage queries), one filters the whole fact table instead of a column, one card scans a 31-million-value timestamp column that is also 59% of the model, and a bi-directional relationship makes a slicer expensive. Fixing them takes the page from {{s04_before_ms|int}} ms to {{s04_after_ms|int}} ms of visual time ({{s04_improvement|pct0}} less) with identical numbers, and shrinks the model from 2.21 GB to about 0.5 GB.
root_cause: Customers Above Average: AVERAGEX(ALL(DimCustomer), [Net Sales]) sits inside FILTER over DimCustomer, so the average over 410k customers is recomputed for every customer. Server Timings: 8,930 ms FE, 4,127 SE queries, CallbackDataID.
Store Sales YTD: FILTER(ALL(FactSales), …) is a table filter: the storage engine materialises all 31.4M rows so the formula engine can test three conditions. Server Timings: one SE query of 2,470 ms.
Last Refreshed: MAX(FactSales[OrderTimestamp]) scans a column with 31.3M distinct values that costs 1,312 MB, 59% of the model, only to show one date.
DimCustomer ↔ FactSales is bi-directional, so the Segment slicer pushes filters from the fact back to the 410k-row customer table on every interaction (1,150 ms, 34 SE queries).
steps: Baseline first, cold cache: clear the cache in DAX Studio, refresh visuals with Performance Analyzer, export. Same machine and same time of day for the after measurement, or the comparison is meaningless.
Rank visuals by DAX query time. Three visuals are about 79% of the page; work on those, not on the slicer that takes 140 ms.
Read Server Timings per query: FE-heavy with thousands of SE queries means row-by-row evaluation; SE-heavy with one big query means too much data scanned or materialised.
Customers Above Average: compute the average once in a variable outside the iterator. Same result, one SE query for the average.
Store Sales YTD: use column filters and the time-intelligence function: KEEPFILTERS on Channel, DATESYTD on the date table. No table scan.
Last Refreshed: drop OrderTimestamp from the model (nothing else uses it) and add a one-row RefreshLog table written by the ETL. Also drop SalesKey, which no visual or relationship uses.
Change DimCustomer → FactSales to single direction. If the slicer must only show segments with sales, filter the slicer visual with a measure (e.g. [Net Sales] > 0) instead.
Regression: run the page's queries before and after in DAX Studio and diff the results. Every value must match.
Measure again cold, write the table, and propose a budget: page under 3 s cold, no visual over 1 s, checked before each release.

artifacts.title: DAX: the rewrites
body: VAR AvgSales = AVERAGEX ( ALL ( DimCustomer[CustomerKey] ), [Net Sales] )   -- once, not per customer
COUNTROWS ( FILTER ( VALUES ( DimCustomer[CustomerKey] ), [Net Sales] > AvgSales ) )
KEEPFILTERS ( FactSales[Channel] = "Store" ),   -- column filter: the storage engine applies it
Last Refreshed = MAX ( RefreshLog[RefreshedAt] )   -- one-row table written by the ETL

artifacts.title: Engineering note
body: - Baseline (cold): 18.2 s wall clock, {{s04_before_ms|int}} ms visual time. Matrix 9.8 s FE-bound (4,127 SE queries, CallbackDataID), Store YTD 2.5 s SE (full fact materialisation), Last Refreshed 2.2 s SE scan of a 31.3M-cardinality column, Segment slicer 1.2 s (bi-directional filtering).
- Fixes: VAR outside iterator; KEEPFILTERS + DATESYTD; OrderTimestamp and SalesKey removed (−1.7 GB, model 2.21 → ~0.5 GB, refresh 41 → ~17 min); relationship single direction.
- After (cold): ~2.6 s wall clock, {{s04_after_ms|int}} ms visual time. Results diffed in DAX Studio: identical.
- Proposed budget: page < 3 s cold, visual < 1 s, model < 1 GB; checked with Performance Analyzer before every release.

communication.executive: The page now opens in under three seconds instead of eighteen, and every number on it is unchanged. The cause was four inefficient calculations added over time, not too little computing power, so there's no extra cost. We've set a speed target that every future change has to meet.
communication.engineer: Three visuals were ~79% of the page: an iterator recomputing AVERAGEX(ALL()) per row (FE, 4,127 SEQ), a table FILTER over the 31M-row fact (SE materialisation) and MAX over a 31M-cardinality datetime (1.3 GB column). Fixed with a variable, column filters with DATESYTD, a RefreshLog table and a single-direction relationship. {{s04_before_ms|int}} → {{s04_after_ms|int}} ms; results diffed equal.

pitfalls: Buying F128. The matrix is formula-engine bound and single-threaded per query: a bigger capacity barely helps it, and it costs every month.
Measuring warm-cache "after" numbers against a cold-cache baseline.
Rewriting measures and changing their results. "Faster but different" is a new incident.
Optimising the 140 ms slicer first because it's easy.

review.junior: Tries the measures one at a time until something feels faster, or asks for a bigger capacity.
review.competent: Uses Performance Analyzer and DAX Studio, fixes the matrix measure and the YTD filter.
review.senior: Baselines cold, classifies each visual as FE or SE bound, fixes all four causes including the model-size and relationship issues, proves results are identical, sets a performance budget and explains why capacity isn't the answer.
review.architect: Adds the performance budget and a BPA rule set to the release process, schedules a quarterly VertiPaq review of the certified model, and makes "urgent" measures go through the same review as any other change.
